To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absorption spectrum of Nd3+ in A-phase Nd2O3 powder, dispersed in KBr, has been measured at 4.2 K by photoacoustic and simultaneous fluorescence excitation spectroscopy.

a new apparatus has been built that allows for the simultaneous high-sensitivity measurement of photoacoustic (PA) and fluorescence (FL) spectra at temperatures from 295 K to 4 K, and that the PA and FL spectra of Nd(3+)-doped Nd(2) O(3) powder have been measured simultaneously and compared.

the photoacoustic spectrum of the (5)D(4) state of Nd3+ in A phase Nd2O3 powder dispersed in a KBR pellet, recorded with a 1 mW laser power, is identical in shape to that of a 10 cm-1 resolution fluorescence excitation spectrum recorded with a 0.5 mW laser power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of high-resolution, variable-temperature photoacoustic spectrometer for use with solid-state samples.
the development of new methods for studying the optical properties of powdered samples at low temperatures.
the development of a new technique that combines the high spectral sensitivity of fluorescence and photoacoustic spectroscopies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work has provided a new and unique approach for studying the electronic states of powdered materials at variable temperature and has shown that the photoacoustic and luminescent spectra of Nd(2) O(3) are consistent with the results of previous studies of this material.
photoacoustic spectroscopy is an excellent method for the investigation of the optical properties of powdered samples, particularly in the near-IR and visible regions of the spectrum.
the apparatus described here is a versatile, high-sensitivity tool for the investigation of the optical spectra of powdered samples at temperatures from 295 K down to 4 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were successful in developing an apparatus that can be used for simultaneous photoacoustic and luminescence measurements on powdered samples at low temperature.
photoacoustic spectroscopy has been demonstrated to have a sensitivity equal to or greater than fluorescence spectroscopy for powdered samples.

we have demonstrated that it is possible to obtain high-quality, simultaneous photoacoustic and laser-induced fluorescence spectra from powdered samples at temperatures down to 4 K, using an apparatus that can be operated in a standard fluorescence spectrometer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoacoustic and photoluminescence spectra of Nd(3+):A-Nd(2)O (3) powder are in excellent agreement, with a maximum difference between the spectra of 0.5 nm.
photoacoustic spectroscopy can be a useful tool in the study of powdered samples at variable temperatures, especially when fluorescence excitation spectra are also recorded simultaneously.
the apparatus described in the paper is a very versatile tool for simultaneous photoacoustic and laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy.
